This article applies the method in `vignette("disruption")` to the whole
nonprofit population: every UEI in the npmatch nonprofit crosswalk (141,420
UEIs), pulled from the USAspending annual award archives for FY2008–FY2026.
That database is not shipped with the package, so the article draws from
pre-computed tables (`data-raw/report_articles.R` copies them in). Two
companion articles go further: [Disruption on the
ledger](disruption-ledger.html) shows what disruption looked like action by action, and
[Obligation trends, FY2026](obligation-trends.html) shows how far new money
fell below trend.

## Which signals moved

Each award is read for the signals `us_disruption_flags()` defines, then
placed in one category, in this order: terminated (formal notice or code),
terminated (quiet end-date cut to within 90 days of the action), reduced
(early de-obligation, ceiling cut, or a shortened schedule), stalled (an
annually funded award whose next funding is more than 120 days overdue, or
stop-work language). The 2023 cohort is the counterfactual: the same rules,
the same window length, two years earlier.

## How much money

Three measures, because a termination notice usually moves no money.
**Obligated at T0** is the award's net obligation on 20 January 2025. **Cash
at stake** is what the outlay model expected the award to pay out in FY2025
and later, given its ledger as it stood on 20 January 2025: the money that
was still to arrive. **De-obligated** and **ceiling cut** are the formal
reductions recorded in the window.

```{=html}
<div class="usr"><div id="t-dollars"></div><div class="finding" id="finding2"></div></div>
```

## By organization size

Size is the organization's IRS revenue (Business Master File), raised to its
largest single year of federal obligations where the BMF figure is smaller,
since federal awards are revenue: small < $1M, medium $1M–$10M, large ≥ $10M.

```{=html}
<div class="usr"><div id="t-size"></div></div>
<p id="size-text"></p>
```

## What this measure misses

- **Freezes with no recorded action.** An award whose payments stop without
  a termination, de-obligation or end-date change is invisible to ledger
  flags. The eight EPA Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund awards in this
  population ($20B obligated to Climate United Fund, Coalition for Green
  Capital, Power Forward Communities and others) have no recorded action of
  any kind between 20 January 2025 and <span class="m-end2"></span>, so they
  are counted as not disrupted here. File C shows why: the money was paid
  out in full by December 2024 (see *What was actually paid*).
- **Subawards.** The annual archives carry prime awards only. Nonprofits
  that receive federal money as subrecipients (through states, universities,
  or other nonprofits) are not measured.
- **Reporting lag.** Contract actions post up to ~90 days late and
  assistance up to ~30, so the last months of the window undercount.
- **Re-awards.** Work moved to a new award (same or different organization)
  reads as a termination of the old one; linking them is a matching problem
  not attempted here.
- **Organization matching.** Organizations come from the npmatch UEI-to-EIN
  crosswalk. A few large recipients are matched to a sibling EIN (Washington
  University → its student-media EIN; MITRE → MITRE Engenuity); the
  federal-revenue floor on size corrects their size class, not their name.

## What was actually paid

The ledger records decisions; outlays record payments. For every disrupted
award, and for a stratified sample of undisrupted ones, the account-level
outlays agencies report in File C were pulled from USAspending
(`POST /awards/funding/`): <span id="p-cov"></span> The comparison uses only
**outlay reporters**, meaning awards with a positive outlay in some quarter
between October 2022 and December 2024, so an agency that does not report
outlays (DoD, largely) never reads as non-payment. Control-sample results are
weighted to the <span id="p-pop"></span> undisrupted non-DoD awards they
represent.

  <div class="chart" id="c-nocash"></div>
</div></div>

## Next steps

- **Freeze detection across all undisrupted awards.** The control sample
  shows that ledger flags miss most State and USAID stoppages; a full File C
  pull of the 120,618 undisrupted awards not yet sampled (about 2 days of API
  time at the observed rate) would count them all.
- **A 2023 payment baseline.** Pulling File C for the 2023 cohort would put
  the no-cash and stopped-paying rates on the same footing as the ledger
  flags.
- **The last failures.** 423 awards still failed after two retries (the API
  rejected about 16% of requests throughout); one more pass should recover
  most.

## Sources

Built with `usaspend` (main @ 22aa2c9: pooled outlay model, dur_bin ×
late_start × short_family; `us_disruption_flags()`). Pipeline scripts 20–27
build the nonprofit database (tables `disruption_active_2025`,
`disruption_active_2023`, `filec_award_quarter`, `payment_stopped`).
Outlays: File C via `us_fetch_outlays()`, pulled 18–19 September 2026.
Universe: grants, cooperative agreements and contracts; loans, direct
payments, insurance and IDV vehicles excluded, and Defense Logistics Agency
supply orders excluded as routine churn.
